nodes.label: ED Safety Calorie Floors (1500 kcal men / 1200 kcal women)
nodes.rationale: Calorie trackers are recognised ED-trigger surfaces; a confidently-wrong personalised number can be worse than an honestly-flagged estimate. Safe floors prevent recommending clinically dangerous deficits.
nodes.norm_label: ed safety calorie floors (1500 kcal men / 1200 kcal women)

nodes.label: One Domain One Icon (Lucide domain icons)
nodes.norm_label: one domain one icon (lucide domain icons)

nodes.label: 4-Tier Transaction Categorizer (finance/categorizer.ts)
nodes.rationale: Cache -> rule -> distilled k-NN -> batched AI tiers keep AI costs near zero for repeat merchants while maintaining accuracy.

nodes.label: Distilled Local k-NN Classifier (merchantClassifier.ts)
nodes.rationale: Char-3-gram TF-IDF + cosine k-NN over 167 anchor strings; zero deps, ~1ms inference. Confidence floor 0.55 before AI escalation.

nodes.label: XP Values Table (5-200 XP per action)
nodes.rationale: Values calibrated to reward meaningful engagement; photo food logging (20 XP) outweighs manual log (5 XP) to incentivize richer data; earning a badge (200 XP) signals major milestone.
nodes.norm_label: xp values table (5-200 xp per action)

nodes.label: Level System (triangular XP curve)
nodes.rationale: Triangular curve xpForLevel(n) = 100*n*(n+1)/2 progressively increases threshold, keeping early levels fast and rewarding while slowing progression at higher levels.

nodes.label: Domain Scores (0-100, rolling 30-day)
nodes.rationale: Weighted rolling average (0.7*current + 0.3*today%) prevents wild swings from a single good/bad day while still reflecting recent activity.

nodes.label: Six Life Engines (Goals/Health/Finance/Career/Social/Polymath)
nodes.rationale: Each engine specialises in one life domain; all feed the Routine Builder (master planner) to synthesise a unified daily plan answering 'What should I do next?'

nodes.label: Privacy by Design (on-device sensitive data)
nodes.rationale: Health logs, blood reports, contacts, transactions are kept on-device to differentiate from cloud-first competitors and address user privacy concerns.

nodes.label: Compaction Hash-Chain Fix (2.4)
nodes.rationale: Option A re-chains the local subsequence with real chainHash so post-compaction rows remain valid chain links; ensures tamper-evidence is preserved after log compaction.

nodes.label: Groq Cheap-Tier Routing (10.2)
nodes.rationale: Groq LPU has far lower TTFT than cross-region Gemini for high-frequency cheap tasks (categorize/briefing/spark/rabbit-hole); OFF by default behind two opt-ins.

nodes.label: Google OAuth Consent Screen Publishing (1.4 runbook)
nodes.norm_label: google oauth consent screen publishing (1.4 runbook)

nodes.label: Google OAuth Secret Server-Side Fix (#1 resolved)
nodes.rationale: Token exchange moved to Worker so GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET never ships in the app bundle; previously the secret was recoverable from any APK/IPA.
nodes.norm_label: google oauth secret server-side fix (#1 resolved)

nodes.label: RLS Deny-by-Default Design (#4 resolved)
nodes.rationale: Tables have ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY with zero policies so only service-role (Worker) can read/write; protects against accidental permissive policies.

nodes.label: Local-First Architecture Pattern
nodes.rationale: Domain data persists on-device in SQLite/localStorage; sensitive data (health, finance, contacts) never leaves the device unencrypted; Cloudflare Worker only proxies AI/auth traffic.

nodes.label: useRotatingPlaceholder Hook
nodes.rationale: Animated, domain-contextual input hints improve perceived onboarding quality; reduced-motion respects accessibility; timer-driven (not animation-callback) prevents blank-state bugs on react-native-web.

nodes.label: Worker as Single Ingress (trust boundary)
nodes.rationale: Neither consumer app nor admin portal queries Supabase Postgres directly; only the Worker holds the service-role key, making it the sole data-plane boundary.

nodes.label: Anonymous Opt-In Telemetry (device_id, no PII)
nodes.rationale: device_id UUID never linked to users.id or email; opt-in OFF by default; allowlisted event vocabulary; 4KB props cap; per-device daily cap.

nodes.label: AI Eval Harness (evals/, 7 suites, 28+ graded cases)
nodes.norm_label: ai eval harness (evals/, 7 suites, 28+ graded cases)

nodes.label: Coverage Ratchet (per-directory floors in jest.config.js)
nodes.rationale: One-way ratchet: floors can only be raised, never lowered without justification; prevents coverage regression while allowing gradual improvement.

nodes.label: CI E2E Auth Failures (chromium project running auth specs without session)
nodes.norm_label: ci e2e auth failures (chromium project running auth specs without session)

nodes.label: Platform.OS Branch Pattern (isWeb)
nodes.rationale: expo-sqlite doesn't work on web; every query file branches on Platform.OS='web' to route to localStorage/Dexie, keeping callers storage-agnostic.

nodes.label: No junction/symlink node_modules Rule
nodes.rationale: On Windows, Remove-Item -Recurse recurses through directory junctions and deletes the real node_modules contents; only real npm ci inside the worktree is safe.

nodes.label: AgentTool Shape (declaration + execute)
nodes.rationale: AgentTool {declaration, execute} is isomorphic to an MCP tool; the hard, valuable part of 'adding MCP' already exists, so retrofitting it later is a thin adapter, not a rewrite.

nodes.label: MCP Server Direction (Worker, synced subset only)
nodes.norm_label: mcp server direction (worker, synced subset only)

nodes.label: MCP Client Direction (on-device, data locality)
nodes.rationale: MCP client hosted on-device (not Worker) preserves data locality; Worker executing tools would break 'Worker executes no tools' invariant.

nodes.label: Two-Tier Detection Architecture (deterministic + LLM on candidates)
nodes.rationale: Cheap deterministic detectors run continuously; LLM reasoning only fires on candidate signals to explain/contextualize. Keeps cost low and latency low; most signals never need an LLM.
nodes.norm_label: two-tier detection architecture (deterministic + llm on candidates)

nodes.label: Action-Taking Coach (gated tool-use)
nodes.rationale: Upgrade chat from read-only to gated tool-use; every action goes through mutation log for auditability and reversibility; confirmation gate for visible/destructive actions.

nodes.label: Intervention Timing Engine (right moment > clever message)
nodes.rationale: Deterministic timing policy (when to surface) + LLM phrasing (how); surfaces P2 cognitive insights at the right moment rather than dumping notifications.
nodes.norm_label: intervention timing engine (right moment > clever message)

nodes.label: Constellation (Explore v2 — first memory graph instance)
nodes.rationale: Explore v2 Constellation validates the 'projection, never source of truth' principle; nodes/edges derived from interests∪sparks∪expeditions, rebuildable.
nodes.norm_label: constellation (explore v2 — first memory graph instance)

nodes.label: Graph as Projection Pattern (rebuildable from spine)
nodes.rationale: Memory nodes/edges derived from signal stream + journal analysis, never authoritative source of truth; drop & re-project yields identical graph; no divergence risk.
nodes.norm_label: graph as projection pattern (rebuildable from spine)

nodes.label: Temporal Query Agent ('what blocked goal X this year?')
nodes.norm_label: temporal query agent ('what blocked goal x this year?')

nodes.label: Salience Decay (keeps graph focused on what currently matters)
nodes.rationale: Nodes lose salience over time unless reinforced; prevents graph explosion and keeps memory graph focused on recent/relevant content rather than accumulating stale context.
nodes.norm_label: salience decay (keeps graph focused on what currently matters)

nodes.label: Constraint Solver (Orchestration)
nodes.rationale: Uses a deterministic scheduler to place fixed/calendar blocks and enforce hard constraints (wake/sleep/work, energy windows), while the LLM proposes what to do. This mirrors the planner's existing deterministic post-guard, scaled up.

nodes.label: Elevation z3 Halo Removal
nodes.rationale: Refined design treats elevation as shadow only — no colored glow. Halo moments belong to motion (BadgeUnlock scene), not resting state.

nodes.label: HexRadar Data Instrument Refinement
nodes.rationale: The refined radar reads as a data instrument, not a hero ornament. Thinner strokes, smaller dots, three grid rings instead of four.

nodes.label: useMotionScale Reduce-Motion Guard
nodes.rationale: Every animation reads useMotionScale() — reduce-motion users see content arrive instantly. This is non-negotiable.

nodes.label: Aurora Refined v2 Hard Rules
nodes.rationale: Nine hard rules: do not touch colors.ts or typography.ts; no new top-level screens; do not edit src/ai, evals, or workers; do not delete design-bundle; use existing motion.ts tokens; use existing radii.ts tokens; run npm test after every phase; respect useMotionScale(); keep snapshots updated.

nodes.label: Aurora Refined v2 Posture: Less Performative, More Inhabited
nodes.rationale: This is not a redesign. Layouts, palette, fonts, component names, and product mental model are preserved. What changes is posture: less performative, more inhabited. Drop neon glow, quiet gamification noise, restrict tinted fills.
nodes.norm_label: aurora refined v2 posture: less performative, more inhabited

nodes.label: Health Engine Strategic Moat
nodes.rationale: LifeOS should not try to out-database MyFitnessPal. Its moat is the master planner + cognition layer + unified event-sourced log across 6 domains. Health features that win are recovery-aware replanning, cross-domain correlations, and a coach that sees the whole life.

nodes.label: Rabbit Hole Tree Persistence: Single JSON Blob
nodes.rationale: Single-row JSON blob wins over two normalized tables. The web render path must read synchronously (localStorage shim returns values, not promises), the deterministic layout must be a pure function of one in-memory object, and the store holds the full nodeMap in memory anyway.
nodes.norm_label: rabbit hole tree persistence: single json blob

nodes.label: No Per-Tap XP (Reward Shape, Not Tap)
nodes.rationale: Kill per-tap XP. Per-milestone idempotent scoring (depth/breadth/synapse pay once each as the shape forms) fits the append-only auto-saved tree. Principle: reward the residue of genuine curiosity, never the act of tapping.
nodes.norm_label: no per-tap xp (reward shape, not tap)

nodes.label: Rabbit Hole Interaction Model (Persistent Append-Only Tree)
nodes.norm_label: rabbit hole interaction model (persistent append-only tree)

nodes.norm_label: rabbit hole badges (deep_diver, cartographer, road_not_taken, connector, archivist)

nodes.label: Production Outcomes vs Synthetic Evals
nodes.rationale: Unlike synthetic eval suites, this report measures real user outcomes: did suggestions the AI produced actually lead to completed routine blocks? It answers the kill/keep question for any task with both single_shot and agent variants.

nodes.label: Protect Chosen Domains — Not Balance Hexagon
nodes.rationale: A domain is a candidate only if it's in the user's primaryDomains. Never flag a non-chosen domain. Imbalance is not automatically bad — a user mid-startup-sprint should be career-heavy. The welcome insight is that a chosen domain has gone quiet; the annoying one is that the hexagon is uneven.
nodes.norm_label: protect chosen domains — not balance hexagon

nodes.label: Three Curiosity Loops (Spark → Rabbit Hole → Expedition → Constellation)
nodes.norm_label: three curiosity loops (spark → rabbit hole → expedition → constellation)

nodes.label: Expedition Progress Set-Union Merge (CRDT-style)
nodes.rationale: completedSteps uses set union of both sides (you can't un-complete by losing a step), currentStep takes max, status = completed wins over active, lastActivityAt takes max. This prevents LWW from losing expedition progress on offline multi-device use.

nodes.label: Broken Priority Feedback Loop (Why It Matters)
nodes.rationale: Priority change is the single strongest intent signal the user can emit — stronger than completing a block or a mood check-in. An adaptive life OS must visibly respond to it, or the user learns that settings are decorative.
nodes.norm_label: broken priority feedback loop (why it matters)

nodes.norm_label: bug-009 — domain taxonomy split (mind vs polymath)

nodes.label: All QA Bugs Closed (Historical Record)
nodes.rationale: Every bug in this handover is now resolved on lifeosv1. This doc is retained as a historical record of the verification + fix-location reasoning, not an active task list.

nodes.label: One Spine, Four Projections (Architecture Thesis)
nodes.rationale: LifeOS does not need five new subsystems. It needs one event-sourced spine (mutation log) and four projections over it: sync, cognition signals, memory graph, and orchestration. All of P1-P5 derive from the same underlying capability: an ordered, durable log of state changes.

nodes.label: Mutation Log as the Highest-Leverage Primitive
nodes.rationale: Build a single primitive — the Mutation Log (CDC) — and derive sync, versioning, cognition signals, and memory from it. This is the moat: an entity-agnostic log that gives new tables sync/versioning/cognition for free.
nodes.norm_label: mutation log as the highest-leverage primitive

nodes.label: Parallel Workstream — Data Leverage, Voice & Production-Readiness
nodes.norm_label: parallel workstream — data leverage, voice & production-readiness

nodes.label: AI Food Recognition: Identify-Then-Lookup Pattern
nodes.rationale: AI photo flow should do identify-then-lookup: let the model name the dish, then look up macros in the bundled DB. Today's recogniseFood asks the model to also estimate macros, which it consistently undershoots by 20-40%.

nodes.label: Provider-Neutral Proxy (/claude Route is Historical)
nodes.rationale: The /claude endpoint name is historical; the request/response body is provider-neutral. LLM_PROVIDER selects the actual provider (currently Gemini by default). API keys are held server-side, never bundled.
